summary: Specifies an extension of OSPFv3 for mobile ad hoc networks, called OSPF-MDR. It adds a MANET interface type that relies on a connected dominating set of routers for flooding. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: In a crowd of moving people, you don't need everyone to shout news. Pick a few well-placed messengers to pass it along, which saves effort.

questions: what is a manet designated router
what is a connected dominating set
subtitle: An OSPFv3 extension that lets a few well-chosen routers do the flooding in mobile wireless networks.

tldr.problem: Existing OSPF interface types do not perform well in mobile ad hoc networks: flooding does not scale, Designated Router election may not converge, and point-to-multipoint interfaces create too many adjacencies.
tldr.mechanism: OSPF-MDR adds a MANET interface type. Routers pick MANET Designated Routers (MDRs) and Backup MDRs that form a connected dominating set, and only those routers flood new LSAs and form most adjacencies.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is Experimental. It reduces flooding and adjacency overhead in dense networks and has been updated by RFC 7038 and RFC 9454.

today: RFC 5614 is an Experimental RFC. It has been updated by RFC 7038 and RFC 9454, so check those for later changes.

sections.title: Why OSPF Needs a MANET Mode
sections.content:
RFC 5614 extends OSPFv3 (RFC 5340) with a new interface type for mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs): broadcast-capable, multihop wireless networks in which routers and hosts can move. It is also applicable to non-mobile mesh networks that use layer-3 routing. It does not preclude the existing OSPF interface types and is stated to be fully compatible with legacy OSPFv3 implementations.

The RFC says existing interface types perform badly here for three reasons: flooding does not scale, the Designated Router election protocol cannot converge in every scenario, and a point-to-multipoint interface produces large numbers of adjacencies.

The approach generalizes the OSPF Designated Router and Backup Designated Router to multihop wireless networks. The generalized routers are called MANET Designated Routers (MDRs) and Backup MDRs, and the result is called OSPF-MDR.
sections.eli5: Regular OSPF works well when everyone can hear everyone. In a field of moving radios, that is not true, so the rules need a version for crowds that keep changing.

sections.title: MDRs, Backup MDRs and Parents
sections.content:
The MDRs form a connected dominating set (CDS): a connected group of routers such that every other router is one hop from it. The MDRs together with the Backup MDRs (BMDRs) form a biconnected CDS if the network itself is biconnected, which adds robustness. Each router decides its own role from information gathered from its neighbors' Hellos.

Each router has an MDR Level: 2 for an MDR, 1 for a BMDR and 0 for an MDR Other. Each non-MDR router picks a neighboring MDR as its Parent and becomes adjacent with it, so every router is attached to the MDR backbone. With biconnected adjacencies, an MDR Other also picks a Backup Parent. Adjacencies are formed only between (Backup) MDRs and a subset of their neighbors, which scales much better than adjacency with every neighbor in dense networks.

A neighbor becomes routable if it is bidirectional and the SPF calculation has produced a route to it. Only routable and Full neighbors can be next hops or appear in a router-LSA. The Parent is advertised in the Hello DR field and the Backup Parent in the Backup DR field.
sections.eli5: A few team captains hear everybody and everybody knows who their captain is. If a captain disappears, a vice-captain steps in.

sections.title: How Routers Choose MDRs
sections.content:
The MDR selection algorithm is distributed and runs on each MANET interface. Routers are ordered by the triplet (RtrPri, MDR Level, RID): Router Priority, then MDR Level, then Router ID. Larger is preferred, so existing MDRs tend to stay MDRs, which lengthens MDR lifetimes and avoids setting up new adjacencies.

In outline, a router that has a larger triplet than all its neighbors makes itself an MDR. Otherwise it finds Rmax, the neighbor with the largest triplet, and becomes an MDR unless every neighbor can be reached from Rmax within MDRConstraint hops through neighbors with a larger triplet than its own. The default of MDRConstraint is 3. A router becomes a BMDR unless every neighbor can be reached from Rmax by two node-disjoint paths using such neighbors.

The algorithm has five phases: build the neighbor connectivity matrix, choose MDR, choose BMDR, choose Parent and Backup Parent, and an optional phase in which an MDR may declare itself non-flooding. It needs 2-hop neighbor information, and the RFC says it can be implemented in O(d^2) time, where d is the number of neighbors. Router Priority can be changed dynamically, for example so that the burden of being an MDR is shared.
sections.eli5: Everybody compares scores with the people nearby. The one with the highest score becomes a captain, unless the other nearby captains can already reach everyone in a few hops.

sections.title: Hellos, Flooding and Acknowledgments
sections.content:
OSPF-MDR uses the OSPFv3 Hello format and appends extra data with link-local signaling (RFC 5613), so each router learns its 2-hop neighborhood. A differential Hello lists only neighbors whose state changed recently, so Hellos can be sent more often without much extra overhead. A full Hello is sent once every 2HopRefresh Hellos, and by default only full Hellos are sent. The new TLV types are the MDR-Hello (14), MDR-DD (15) and MDR-Metric (16) TLVs.

When an MDR receives a new LSA on a MANET interface it floods it back out the same interface unless that is unnecessary. A BMDR waits for the BackupWaitInterval (default 0.5 second) and floods only if some neighbor did not flood or acknowledge the LSA and is not known to be covered by another neighbor that did. An MDR Other never floods an LSA back out the receiving interface. Reliability comes from retransmitting LSAs along adjacencies.

All Link State Acknowledgments are multicast. A new LSA is acknowledged, and so is a duplicate received as unicast, but a duplicate received as multicast is not. Flooding an LSA back out the same interface counts as an implicit acknowledgment.
sections.eli5: Only the captains repeat the news out loud. Vice-captains listen for a moment, and repeat it only if somebody nearby clearly missed it.

sections.title: Tunable Interface Parameters
sections.content:
The MANET interface defaults are HelloInterval 2 seconds, RouterDeadInterval 6 seconds and RxmtInterval 7 seconds. The default configuration uses uniconnected adjacencies (AdjConnectivity = 1) and partial-topology LSAs that give shortest-path routing (LSAFullness = 1), which the RFC calls the most scalable configuration that still provides shortest paths.

AdjConnectivity chooses how many adjacencies to form: 0 is full-topology adjacencies, 1 a connected set and 2 a biconnected set. LSAFullness chooses what each router advertises in its router-LSA. Routing along shortest paths is provided if and only if every router uses 1, 2 or 4.

When the average number of neighbors is large (for example above 50), differential Hellos are recommended, with 2HopRefresh set to 3. Good performance is reported in simulated mobile networks of up to 160 nodes with the default configuration and differential Hellos, and up to 200 nodes with minimal LSAs. Routers need not use identical parameter values.
sections.eli5: There are dials on the radio, such as how often to check in and how much detail to share. The factory settings are chosen to work well for most crowds.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Like OSPFv3, OSPF-MDR can use the IPv6 Authentication Header and Encapsulating Security Payload for authentication, integrity and confidentiality, as described in RFC 4552. These mechanisms do not protect against compromised, malfunctioning or misconfigured (Byzantine) routers.

The extension introduces no new threats, but the wireless medium and the lack of infrastructure make some attacks easier, including sniffing, traffic analysis, interference, spoofing, falsification and overloading. Confidentiality protects against sniffing but not traffic analysis.

RFC 4552 requires manual keying, so all routers on one MANET must use the same key, and compromise of any one router leaves all of them open to impersonation. When a routing domain mixes MANET and fixed networks, border routers are advised to separate them using different OSPF areas or separate OSPF instances.
sections.eli5: Radio signals can be overheard by anyone close enough, so the messages need a lock. A single shared key is easy to use, but if one person loses it, everyone is at risk.

items.label: MDR
items.desc: Part of the connected dominating set. Floods LSAs and is its own Parent.

items.label: Backup MDR
items.desc: Provides backup flooding when neighboring MDRs fail.

items.label: MDR Other
items.desc: Neither an MDR nor a Backup MDR. Never floods an LSA back out the receiving interface.
